statement: When two independent, simultaneously-openable UI surfaces present overlapping or duplicate information about the SAME thing, the fix is to consolidate them into ONE surface (one owns the state, the other becomes a control that opens/focuses it), never to add containment (a backdrop, a z-index bump, an opacity change) around the extra surface. Containment can make the SYMPTOM (visual overlap) disappear while leaving the actual defect — two competing surfaces — in place, where it can resurface as a worse regression (e.g. a full-viewport backdrop combining with the surface underneath to look like one broken modal).
notes: First observed in components/journey/JourneyRunSurface.tsx: the header's own 'Evidence N/M' popover duplicated a subset of what StageReceiptsDrawer already showed further down the same stage body. A first fix pass (commit 3ba5ef913) added a fixed inset-0 backdrop to contain the popover's overlap with the drawer — this made the deployed experience WORSE (a full-viewport translucent layer combined with the drawer's own content to look like one broken modal), because the underlying two-surfaces-for-one-concept problem was untouched.

The actual fix (2026-09-06) removed the header's own popover entirely and made its control drive the ONE remaining surface (StageReceiptsDrawer) via controlled open/onOpenChange props — any information the removed surface uniquely showed (here, missing-evidence pills) was migrated INTO the surviving surface, never dropped.

Generalizes beyond this one case: any 'add a backdrop / raise the z-index / dim everything else' fix for an overlap between two content-bearing UI elements is a signal to ask whether they are actually the same concern rendered twice, before reaching for containment.

occurrences.site: components/journey/JourneyRunSurface.tsx — header Evidence popover vs. StageReceiptsDrawer
occurrences.defect: A fixed inset-0 backdrop was added to contain the header popover's overlap with StageReceiptsDrawer underneath, combining with the drawer's own visible content to read as one broken, translucent modal in production.

canaries.assertion: a real Chromium browser, driven against the real rendered DOM styled with the project's own compiled Tailwind CSS, confirms no fixed full-viewport layer exists (open or closed), the header control never overlaps the (now sole) drawer, and receipt cards render contained inside it.
